title: feat(load-generator): replace Locust with k6
author: mwimpelberg28
body:
Closes/addresses #3503

## What this PR does

Replaces the Locust-based load generator with one built on [k6](https://k6.io/).

### Load generator
- New k6 script (`src/load-generator/script.js`) reproducing the previous user
  journeys as two scenarios: an HTTP `load` scenario and a `browser` scenario
  (via the k6 browser module) that exercises the frontend like a real user.
- A small custom xk6 extension (`src/load-generator/xk6-otel`) bridges k6's JS
  runtime to the OTel Go SDK so the script can emit spans for each user journey
  and propagate W3C trace context to backend services.
- The runtime image is based on `grafana/k6:2.1.0-with-browser` (validated
  Chromium), with our custom k6 binary copied over the stock one. The xk6 build
  and go.mod are pinned to k6 v2.1.0 to match the base image.
- `loadGeneratorBrowserVUs` supports `0` to drop the browser scenario entirely
  (k6 launches Chromium per browser-VU iteration regardless of the traffic flag,
  so omitting the scenario at launch is the only way to reclaim that CPU).

### Supporting changes
- Removed the Locust web UI route from Envoy and the corresponding
  `http://localhost:8080/loadgen/` links from the Makefile and CONTRIBUTING.md
  (k6 has no web UI).
- Increased the otel-collector memory limit from 200M to 400M. The browser
  scenario adds `frontend-web` spans on top of full-scope backend telemetry, and
  the collector's `memory_limiter` (`limit_percentage: 80`) would trip at 200M
  under that combined load and intermittently refuse data, causing `frontend-web`
  traces to go missing. 400M gives enough headroom.
- Fixed collector CORS (`allowed_headers` for `traceparent`/`baggage`) so the
  browser SDK's OTLP export isn't rejected by preflight.
- Fixed load-generator service dependencies (depend on `frontend-proxy`, its
  actual target) and browser sandbox/startup crashes.

### Resource impact
k6 uses substantially less CPU and memory than Locust for equivalent load — see
the benchmarks in the PR comments (roughly ~4x lighter on the browser workload).

comments.author: mwimpelberg28
comments.text:
CodeQL flagged all uses of `Math.random()` in `script.js` as insecure randomness. Fixed in 75b6605.

Changes:
- Replaced `uuid4()` with `crypto.randomUUID()` (Web Crypto API, built into k6 v2)
- Added a `cryptoRandom()` helper using `crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint32Array(1))` and replaced all remaining `Math.random()` calls (`randomChoice()`, `selectTask()`, sleep jitter, browser task selection)
